column2: ENGLISH

The sky goes black in the west and the sea rises to meet it. The crews strike the sails and lash themselves to the masts, and the bosun swears this is the worst blow he has seen in twenty years at sea. He says that every time, but this time he is pale when he says it.

The Sea of Claws earns its name. A storm comes down out of the north with ice in it, and the waves stand as tall as a temple. Ships vanish into the troughs and come up again with fewer men on deck. Somewhere ahead the grey shapes of icebergs drift in the murk.
Hold the course and ride it out.
Pour wine into the sea for Manann!
Run for the nearest coast.

Long low hulls come out of the sea-mist, oars beating, shields on the rails and a dragon's head on every prow. The Norscans have been waiting. They howl to their gods across the water and the first arrows fall short of the deck.
Board them before they board us!
Throw them a chest of silver and let them go.
Crowd on every sail and outrun them.

The lookout screams from the masthead. Something vast is moving under the water off the starboard bow, a shape longer than three ships, and when it breaks the surface the sea around it is full of drowned timber and dead fish. The old hands make the sign of Manann. The young ones want to hunt it.
Harpoons! We hunt it.
Steer well clear of that thing.

For days the fleet follows the beast's trail. Wreckage, an empty longboat, the half of a whale and a slick of blood that the gulls will not touch. The crews are tired and frightened, and the cold is getting into everyone. The trail goes on into the north.
Press on. It cannot be far.
Enough. Turn the fleet about.

It comes up under the lead ship without warning. A head like a reef, eyes like lanterns of green fire and a mouth that could swallow a cog whole. Timber screams, men fall into the water and the harpoon crews run to their winches. This is the moment the hunt was for.
Loose everything we have!

The leviathan thrashes for an hour with a dozen harpoons in it, and then it rolls over and is still. The crews cut its teeth out with axes, each one as long as a man's arm, and the whole fleet drinks to [Root.GetTitledFirstName], the slayer of the Sea of Claws.
Hang its jaw from the masthead!

The beast drags two ships under with it and smashes a third into kindling. [Root.GetTitledFirstName] is thrown across the deck when the monster strikes and is pulled out of the freezing water half dead. When the survivors look again the sea is empty and the leviathan is gone.
Curse the thing. Make for port.

A pirate captain rows across under a white rag on a boathook. He has a dozen ships, he says, fast ones with good crews, and he is tired of being hunted. Grant him a pardon in our realm's name, and he will fly our colours and hunt our enemies instead.
Grant him amnesty. We can use his ships.
Send him away.
Hang him from the yardarm.

The pirate captain pardoned years ago has kept his word. His ships have taken a dozen enemy merchantmen and sunk two raiders, and the lords of the coast speak well of him. Some say he has even started going to temple.

The pirate captain pardoned years ago has sailed off in the night, taking his ships, his crews and the silver from the harbour treasury with him. A note was left nailed to the harbourmaster's door. It thanks [Root.GetTitledFirstName] for the hospitality.
Well.

A tall white ship with sails like a swan's wing comes alongside, faster than anything in our fleet. The Asur aboard are polite, distant and plainly amused by our ships. They offer to trade, and one of them, a mage in robes of blue and silver, asks to take passage with us for reasons of his own.
Trade with them.
Win them over for Erengrad's Elven Quarter.
Give the mage passage and listen to him.

A line of longships lies across the strait, oars up, waiting. A Norscan jarl stands in the prow of the biggest and calls across the water that these are his seas and that every ship pays him to pass. He names a price. It is not even an unreasonable one.
Pay the toll.
We pay no jarl!
Swear a trade-friendship with the jarl.

Warships with white stars painted on their sails come up from the south. They are the Knights of the White Star of Erengrad, sworn to Ulric and to keeping the Sea of Claws clear of raiders. Their commander offers to see our fleet safely through these waters.
Gladly. We sail with the White Star.
We need no Ulrican to guard us.
A wave breaks over the deck and when it is gone a sailor is in the water, already falling behind the ship. His shipmates run to the rail and shout, and look to [Root.GetTitledFirstName].
Go in after him myself!
Throw him a line!
He belongs to Manann now. Hold the course.
A fever is running through the crews. Men shake in their hammocks and the ship's surgeon has nothing left to give them. The nearest port is days away and out of our way.
Put in at the nearest port.
Press on. The sea air will cure them.
Meanwhile at the Palace...

I am enjoying a late supper in my palace at [Root.Capital.GetName], sampling new wines brought in from the provinces, when a distant explosion rolls across the city. Windows shatter and the chandelier above begins to sway as the shockwave hits a moment later. Dust trickles from the rafters, and to my dismay some of it lands in my wine.\n\nI hurry to a balcony over the city and see a fierce fire raging in one of the warehouses by the docks. The water of the harbour itself is ablaze, and the flames have already spread to several ships at anchor. While their crews abandon them, the harbour is rocked by a string of smaller blasts from the burning warehouse.
This must be investigated!
Pretty, but I need a new glass of wine.
You open an investigation into this strange explosion.
Sifting through the Ashes

The next day, when the fire has finally burned out, I inspect the ruins of the warehouse with my guards. My advisers tell me that it held the realm's store of liquid fire, the sea fire that the engineers of Tilea learned to brew from the notebooks of Leonardo of Miragliano. It burns even on water, and it has saved this port from more than one fleet of corsairs.\n\nThe damage to the warehouse and the harbour is the least of my worries. No trace remains of the formula, a closely guarded secret of the engineers' guild for three hundred years, nor of the alchemists who worked in the warehouse. Without them, the supply of sea fire is cut off.
This is a disaster!
You return to the palace...
Pirates Sighted!

Strange reports come in of a pirate fleet in the Tilean Sea, out of Sartosa by the look of it. If the witnesses can be believed, the pirates burn any ship that will not strike its colours with a fire spewed from the prows of their galleys. Could these pirates somehow have the formula for sea fire?\n\nIf this weapon falls into the hands of every corsair and enemy of the realm, we will lose a great edge! My admiral has drawn up a plan to send a small squadron to hunt the brigands down. My spymaster has another plan: plant spies in every port from Sartosa to Magritta until they find their way into the pirate band and uncover its hideout.
Alert all commands. Send out the fleet.
A squadron prowls the Tilean Sea for the pirates.
Send in the spies.
Battle off Sartosa!

News from the sea! The squadron I sent out has forced the pirate fleet to battle. In a hard-fought fight off Sartosa, my sailors boarded and took one of the pirate galleys. They lost several ships to sea fire, but their prize is even now coming in to the harbour.\n\nAmong the captured pirates is a young woman named Despina. This vixen was apparently the galley's captain, and she claims to be the daughter of the pirate king himself, a Myken corsair named Kyrillos. If that is true, I may have a hostage worth her weight in gold...

They lost several ships to sea fire, but their prize is even now coming in to the harbour.\n\nAmong the captured pirates is a woman named Eleni. My men tell me this old harridan has quite the temper, and that she claims to be the wife of the pirate king himself, a Myken corsair named Kyrillos. If that is true, I may have a hostage worth her weight in gold...
Guards, treat her well. We may need her.

News from the sea! The squadron I sent out has been beaten by the pirate fleet! In a hard-fought fight off Sartosa, the pirates ambushed my sailors and set their ships alight with sea fire. A single ship escaped and has just limped back into port.\n\nIt is clearer than ever that this weapon cannot be left in the hands of savages and cutthroats. Something must be done!
Yes... but what?
Word from the Spies!

News from the sea! One of my spies got himself taken on as an oarsman in the pirate fleet and spent a month chained to a bench. The secret of their sea fire was kept to their officers, and he never learned where their hideout lies.\n\nBut there is good news. He brought a prisoner with him when he escaped: a young woman named Despina. This vixen was apparently the captain of his galley, and she claims to be the daughter of the pirate king himself, a Myken corsair named Kyrillos. If that is true, I may have a hostage worth her weight in gold...

The secret of their sea fire was kept to their officers, and he never learned where their hideout lies.\n\nBut there is good news. He brought a prisoner with him when he escaped: a woman named Eleni. My spy tells me this old harridan has quite the temper, and that she claims to be the wife of the pirate king himself, a Myken corsair named Kyrillos. If that is true, I may have a hostage worth her weight in gold...

News from the sea! My spymaster sets down a sack that an unknown courier left at the gate this morning. Its contents are tipped out on the table before me: the severed heads of every agent I sent to infiltrate the pirate fleet.\n\nThese are no simple cutthroats. These pirates are a threat to the whole realm. Something must be done!
You await further developments.
The Letter

A letter was found this morning nailed to the palace doors. It seems to be written in blood, most likely that of the dead guard left impaled on a spear in the garden. It reads:

'You have something of mine, and I have something of yours. I propose a trade. On the back of this letter you will find a map to a barren islet off Sartosa. Bring my Despina, and I will bring the formula of your sea fire, and the only alchemist left alive who knows how to brew it.

Signed,
King Kyrillos the Magnanimous'

A letter was found this morning nailed to the palace doors. It seems to be written in blood, most likely that of the dead guard left impaled on a spear in the garden. It reads:

'So you have my wife. Keep her if you like, but you will still pay. I propose a trade. On the back of this letter you will find a map to a barren islet off Sartosa. Bring Eleni and plenty of gold, and I will bring the formula of your sea fire, and the only alchemist left alive who knows how to brew it.

Signed,
King Kyrillos the Magnanimous'

'Enough games, [Root.GetTitle]. I have something you want, and you must know by now that it cannot be taken by force of arms. I propose a trade. On the back of this letter you will find a map to a barren islet off Sartosa. Bring plenty of gold, and I will bring the formula of your sea fire, and the last alchemist alive who knows how to brew it.

Signed,
King Kyrillos the Magnanimous'
An excellent chance for an ambush...
I cannot risk crossing this man.
You prepare an ambush for the pirate king.
You decide to follow the pirate's instructions to the letter.
The Deal

I set sail with a small fleet for the islet Kyrillos named in his letter. As we draw near, I order the rest of the ships to scatter and cover every way out while my flagship goes in alone. The pirate king is already waiting on the barren rock, and I land with Despina and a handful of trusted guards. Kyrillos stands among his brigands.\n\n'Release the girl,' he bellows. 'Ye shall have yer alchemist and yer formula back, on my honour.' The pirates push forward a frail old man clutching a scroll, and I do the same with Kyrillos' daughter. 'My apologies about the warehouse and the docks,' the pirate king says with a grin. 'We had to cover our tracks.' The deal done, both sides make for their ships.

Eleni protests loudly, but the pirates push forward a frail old man clutching a scroll, and I grudgingly hand over the gold. The deal done, I take Eleni back to my ship and both sides depart.

The deal is done.
Your ship hoists its sails.
Coming Home

We set course for home, and my men confirm that the old man is indeed one of the missing alchemists. The formula he carries seems genuine too. Before we round the last headland we meet the rest of the fleet: the ambush worked! They caught Kyrillos and his galley, and after a fierce fight took both the pirate king and his daughter.\n\nWith the secret of sea fire back in the realm's hands, and the thieves who stole it chained in the hold, this matter can at last be laid to rest. As [Root.Capital.GetName] comes into view across the water, I take a deep breath of sea air. It is good to be [Root.GetTitle].
